title: The Duke's Secret Chess Name
body: In 1616, a German duke named Augustus wanted to publish a translation of a famous chess book. Instead of using his royal name, he made up a secret pen name, Gustavus Selenus, to sign his work.

variants.lucy: Long ago in the year 1616, a gentle German duke named Augustus worked on a special book about chess. He translated the wise words so everyone could read them, but he did not want his royal title on the cover. Instead, he chose a beautiful secret name, Gustavus Selenus, to sign his lovely pages.
variants.luca: Imagine a powerful ruler sneaking around to write a book! Duke Augustus wanted to share a legendary chess guide, but he needed a brilliant disguise. He cooked up a secret identity, Gustavus Selenus, and slipped it onto the cover like a spy on a mission.

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
